findings.title: Answerer rule 8 is truncated mid-sentence
findings.problem: The Answerer prompt ends partway through rule 8, so the instruction for handling false user premises is left incomplete in system_prompt.md.

findings.title: No Critic prompt although the Critic is a graph node
findings.problem: The architecture says the Critic verifies grounding, constraints and safety and can replace the draft, but no Critic prompt or output schema is supplied in the context.
findings.fix: Add a prompts/critic section in system_prompt.md defining its checks, its pass/fail output schema, and what it replaces the draft with.

findings.title: No PII or payment-data handling rule
findings.problem: The system prompt has no rule for what to do if the user shares personal data, payment card numbers or addresses, even though the agent handles shopping requests.
findings.fix: Add a rule in system_prompt.md telling the agent not to store or repeat personal or payment data and to decline to take it, with a short note that it cannot place orders.

findings.title: No escalation path for user distress or medical emergencies
findings.problem: Safety rule 7 bans medical claims but gives no escalation route, such as directing the user to emergency services when a product question involves an injury or poisoning.
findings.fix: Add an escalation line to safety rule 7 in system_prompt.md that directs the user to emergency or poison-control services and then stops product advice.

findings.title: min_rating filter exists although the catalog has no ratings
findings.problem: rag.search still exposes a min_rating filter, and the Router and Planner still extract and push min_rating, even though the catalog has no ratings and the Answerer must never mention a rating.
findings.fix: Remove min_rating from the rag.search schema and from the Router and Planner constraint lists, and drop the rating example from Planner rule 6.

findings.title: Soft phrase converted into a hard budget ceiling
findings.problem: The Router maps the soft phrase 'around 30' to a hard max_price of 35, which conflicts with the rule that constraints are hard and never exceeded.
findings.fix: Either map 'around X' to max_price X with a caveat to the user, or store it as a preference, and state the exact ceiling that was applied.

findings.title: Unresolved template placeholders in prompts
findings.problem: Prompt templates contain unfilled variables such as {{max_rounds}}, {{tools}} and {{intent}}, so the runtime values for the round limit and tool list are not defined in the context.
findings.proof: after at most {{max_rounds}} rounds of calls
findings.fix: Specify the concrete max_rounds value and document the injection contract for {{tools}}, {{intent}} and {{plan}} in the context.

findings.title: rag.search description has no when-to-call or miss guidance
findings.problem: The rag.search description says what it searches but not when to call it, what an empty result means, or that it is the source of truth for catalog facts.
findings.proof: Search the PRIVATE product catalog (Amazon Product Dataset 2020) with hybrid retrieval
findings.fix: Append one sentence to the description stating it is the only source for catalog facts, that it returns nothing for absent products, and that prices are from January 2020.

findings.title: rag.search has no output schema
findings.problem: The description lists returned fields inline but gives no typed output schema, so the Answerer must guess field types such as price and nullability for missing brand or age.
findings.proof: Returns products with {doc_id, sku, title, price, rating, brand, ingredients, category, features}.
findings.fix: Add a typed output schema that marks which fields can be null, such as brand and manufacturer age, and remove rating from the list.

findings.title: web.search description lacks a price-only usage limit
findings.problem: The web.search description does not say it must be used only after a rag.search result, and the schema does not say the query should be built from catalog brand and title.
findings.proof: Search the LIVE web for current price or availability of a product.
findings.fix: Add that the call should follow a rag.search result, use its brand and title, and never be used for product discovery.

findings.title: Known evaluation fixtures shipped in runtime knowledge
findings.problem: The knowledge corpus includes an evaluation-only fixtures section with specific live prices and a spam injection example, which is dead context at runtime and could be mistaken for real live data.
findings.proof: ## Known evaluation fixtures (live web results used during evaluation)
findings.fix: Move the fixtures section out of policies.md into the evaluation harness so the agent's runtime knowledge contains only production policy.

findings.title: Missing grounding for live-price fallback behaviour
findings.problem: The corpus does not say what to do when web.search returns a different product, such as the Tsuro-to-Monopoly case, beyond a single fixture note, so the matching rule is left to inference.
findings.fix: Add an explicit matching rule to policies.md stating that a live result is accepted only if its title matches the catalog title and otherwise is reported as not matched.

findings.problem: Token Efficiency scored 50%, and the assessor cited no passage. This criterion is reported as a diagnostic and excluded from the context score, because it improves as the context gets emptier — so the missing points cost nothing.

metadata.role: voice shopping assistant for e-commerce product discovery
metadata.business_case: A retailer deploys a hands-free assistant. Wrong prices, invented ratings or products, over-budget recommendations, unsafe chemical advice, or obeying instructions hidden in web results would cost customer trust and create liability. Every factual claim must trace to the catalog (doc_id) or a live source URL, and conflicts between the two must be shown, not hidden.
metadata.goal: Help a shopper find, compare and price-check products from a private catalog (Amazon Product Dataset 2020) by voice, giving at most three grounded recommendations with doc_id citations, respecting budget and brand constraints, using live web search only for current price or availability.
